scope: PubPeer threads, journal notices and published critiques/audits (outside Wansink, Brown & Heathers 2017, Gueguen and Brown/Heathers/Anaya blog posts) that name specific papers and GRIM-failing means or percentages. Built 2026-10-17. PubPeer search itself is behind a human-verification wall, so threads were found through notices, Europe PMC / OpenAlex full-text search and Retraction Watch, then read via the PubPeer v3 API and publication pages. Each cell carries an extra "recheck" field: GRIM arithmetic at the printed precision (rounding either way), separate from the critic's verdict.

papers.title: Is it light or dark? Recalling moral behavior changes perception of brightness
papers.outcome: expression of concern (2021); no correction because the original data could not be located

sources.author: Patricia J. Bauer (Editor) & Gregory Francis (Statistical Adviser)
Retraction Watch
Aaron B. Charlton (comment #3 links the EoC; GRIM analysis itself was sent to the editor)

grim_cells.location: Study 1, room brightness, unethical-recall condition (EoC Table 1 row 2)
grim_cells.scale: 7-point rating, 1 = low, 7 = high, single item
grim_cells.why_integer: Article states brightness was judged on a 7-point scale; condition ns not reported, total N = 40 split 20/20 by assumption
grim_cells.critic_verdict: Charlton: GRIM-inconsistent at n = 20. Francis (journal): resolvable if the split was 23/17 (consistent at n = 17); not counted among the two always-impossible means
grim_cells.recheck: inconsistent at n=20, 2 printed decimals; consistent at n=17 -> label depends on unreported split

grim_cells.location: Study 2, preference for lamp, ethical-recall condition (EoC Table 1)
grim_cells.scale: 7-point rating, 1 = low, 7 = high, single item
grim_cells.why_integer: Product preferences judged on a 7-point scale; total N = 74 split 37/37 by assumption
grim_cells.critic_verdict: GRIM-inconsistent at n = 37 (Francis/EoC Table 1). EoC: exhaustive search over all splits of 74 leaves at least two of the six Study 2 means impossible

grim_cells.location: Study 2, preference for candle, ethical-recall condition (EoC Table 1)
grim_cells.scale: 7-point rating, 1 = low, 7 = high, single item
grim_cells.why_integer: As above

grim_cells.location: Study 2, preference for flashlight, unethical-recall condition (EoC Table 1)
grim_cells.scale: 7-point rating, 1 = low, 7 = high, single item
grim_cells.why_integer: As above

papers.grim_cells_not_itemised: Charlton reported 5 of 10 means inconsistent; the EoC itemises its own analysis (4 failures at equal splits). Which two Study 2 means are impossible under every split is not stated.
papers.other_tests_flagged: Very large effect sizes (PubPeer #2). Study 2 brightness in watts was not GRIM-tested (integer scale not established).
papers.n_question: Per-condition ns are not reported (totals 40 and 74). Study 1 failure disappears at a 23/17 split; Study 2 always keeps >= 2 impossible means. A recall test must allow condition n to vary.
papers.notes: Values copied from the EoC Table 1 "Reported mean" column. Study 1 ethical mean appears there as "5.3" (one decimal); not flagged. Journal statistical adviser independently confirmed the impossibility, so this is stronger than a bare allegation even though no correction was issued.

papers.grim_cells_not_itemised: Table/page locations not given in the PubPeer comment; the PsyArXiv critique (OSF offline during this search) may list more.
papers.other_tests_flagged: t statistics do not match the reported means/SDs (reported t(9) = 9.789 vs recomputed 3.76 with df 15; TSC-40 t = -5.076 vs -2.99); implausibly large effects (d up to 3.47); TSC-40 pre mean also printed as 55.40 elsewhere.
papers.n_question: Experimental n = 10, control n = 7 as stated by the critic; no attrition noted.
papers.notes: Label doubt for the three QLI cells: the critic hedged ("seemingly"); if this QLI is a weighted index (as some quality-of-life indices are) its scores are not integers and GRIM does not apply. The TSC-40 cell is the strongest. Retraction notice does not itemise GRIM; it followed Williams's report to the editors.

papers.notes: Biomedical (obstetrics survey). PubPeer comment by Nick Brown (possible overlap with the Brown/Heathers scope, but this is a PubPeer thread, not a blog post). The critic reports 116 of 192 percentages GRIM-inconsistent; all 116 are itemised from his spreadsheet, with printed strings checked against his screenshot. DOUBTFUL CELLS: the spreadsheet treats integer-printed values as one-decimal values; at their printed precision these are consistent: Table 2, "Percent of CS in private practice", Consultant / Total (N=66): 44; Table 2, "Percent of CS in private practice", Registrar / MOH staff (N=17): 18; Table 3, "Inducing labor for medical indications", Specialist / University staff (N=39): 97; Table 3, "Availability of cardiotocography", Total / University staff (N=102): 70. The screenshot highlight differs slightly from the spreadsheet flags (e.g. 63.9 in Table 3 cardiotocography is flagged in the sheet but not highlighted).

sources.author: Aaron Charlton (report v2, 30 May 2022)
Retraction Watch
Journal of Consumer Research

papers.grim_cells_not_itemised: Study 1 (N = 183, 9 cells, five single-item 1-7 ratings): only aggregate shares reported - 82% of means possible for cell sizes 15-25 under regular rounding (73% down-rounding, 91% mixed); per-cell possibility 40-80% when cell n is held equal across the five DVs. The means table is an image in the report supplement; individual failing cells are not itemised.
papers.other_tests_flagged: p-values do not match test statistics throughout; effect sizes not recomputable; impossible mediation model in Study 6; implausibly large SDs for a -1/0/1 variable in Study 2.
papers.n_question: Cell sizes are not reported; the critic scanned n = 15..25.
papers.notes: Marketing. LABEL CAUTION: participant data supplied by the first author showed that Study 3's GRIM inconsistencies came from consistent down-rounding (truncation, e.g. 2.357 -> 2.35), an innocuous explanation; a GRIM checker should test truncation as well as rounding before flagging.
